issues: Line 311: the share `text` JS string contains the JSX-encoded entity `I'm building AI Video Studio` — because it's inside a plain JS string literal (not JSX), the literal characters 'I'm' get URL-encoded into the LinkedIn summary rather than being rendered as an apostrophe. LinkedIn users will see 'I'm building…' as raw text in the pre-filled post. Fix: change `I'm` to `I'm` (escape the JS quote with backticks or a backslash — the surrounding literal is a backtick template so a plain apostrophe is safe). Same issue applies to the H2 headline on line 301 `let's change that` — but there it IS inside JSX so it renders correctly; only line 311's occurrence is a bug.

action_items: OPTIONAL polish (non-blocking, cosmetic on LinkedIn share preview): in /app/frontend/src/pages/AdminPanel.jsx line 311, replace the two occurrences of the string `I'm` inside the `text` template literal with a plain apostrophe `I'm`. The HTML entity is meaningless inside a JS string (only meaningful in JSX/HTML) and will URL-encode as literal 'I'm' in the LinkedIn share summary. Everything else is green.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py /api/admin/sanity (lines 426-515) — clean impl. Uses $toLower for case-insensitive dup grouping ($group._id = {$toLower: '$email'}), properly caps sample arrays ($limit 50 for dups; orphans capped via Python slice [:25]), pct math uses round(x, 2) with a zero-guard on total_sessions. The orphan detection joins waitlist.email ↔ analytics_events(waitlist_submit|waitlist_success).properties.email (lowercased on both sides) and checks that at least one of the collected session_ids appears in the set of page_view session_ids — correct. Only minor smell: the endpoint loads ALL waitlist rows into memory to compute orphans; fine at current scale (~60 rows) but consider a pipeline aggregation once scale grows past a few thousand.

AdminPanel.jsx sanity-verdict threshold logic (line 224/228) — the healthy condition is `orphans + duplicates == 0 AND unattributed_pct < 25`. This matches the spec. UX-wise: with the current live DB (0 orphans, 0 dups, 26.23% untagged) the verdict correctly shows '⚠ Review recommended', because 26.23 ≥ 25 — the threshold is inclusive-of-25 on the amber side. That's a reasonable choice but worth documenting; a founder seeing exactly 25.00% would find it counter-intuitive that it's flagged. Consider `<= 25` if you want to be lenient at the boundary. Non-blocking.

AdminPanel.jsx line 311 — `I'm` inside a JS string (not JSX) is a subtle bug (see design_issues). No functional impact on click routing, only affects the LinkedIn share preview text. Also on line 301 the JSX `let's` is correct (JSX context).

AdminPanel.jsx attribution matrix tooltips (lines 601-609) — nice UX: 3 distinct tooltip templates covering (a) overflow (signups > sessions), (b) normal cells, and (c) sessions==0 but signups>0 or both zero. Plain-English wording is clear. Green ≥ 20% threshold and amber overflow visual mapping are consistent with the footnote legend.

ProjectView.jsx warning copy (lines 154-160) — softening from 'Video file not found' → 'Video failed to load' + 'network, decoding or storage issue' is exactly right; the <video onError> handler fires for ALL load failures (404, decode error, network error, unsupported codec), so the previous copy was misleading in edge cases. Iter-9/10 hooks-order regression stays fixed — useState(videoMissing) and the reset useEffect remain above the `if (!p) return` early return.

server.py /api/admin/sanity does not gate the aggregation on a `since` window — with 6+ months of data at scale, the analytics_events $group over all page_view events could get expensive. Consider a default 90-day window with a `days` query param.

rca of the issue: No issues to RCA — all iter-11 changes verified working end-to-end. The one minor cosmetic issue (AdminPanel.jsx line 311 `I'm` inside JS string literal) has a trivial 1-char fix: replace `I'm` with `I'm` (or use `I\u2019m` for the curly apostrophe). Root cause is the same JSX-vs-JS confusion that produced iter-10's hooks-order violation — a copy-paste of an HTML entity from a JSX context into a plain JavaScript template literal. No user-visible impact until someone actually clicks 'Share beta on LinkedIn' from the waitlist empty state (which requires the founder to have 0 signups).
